title: Legal AI Vendor Pre-Demo Scorecard: Pre-demo Written Responses for Public Defender Evaluation
pub: UC Berkeley Center for Criminal Law & Justice, Defenders Meet AI
author: UC Berkeley Center for Criminal Law & Justice · BearisterAI

dom.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment

st.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment
st.an: The source offers narrow, pre-demo vendor claims about privacy, citations, search architecture, recall and robustness, while the programme frames them for evaluation rather than endorsement. It neither establishes nor rejects the cluster’s broader proposition that jagged capabilities require selective deployment, human verification and operating-model redesign; the absence of test methodology and completed independent assurance further limits inference.

st.t: Reliable delivery: Legal engineering bridges capability and service
st.an: The scorecard reinforces the cluster’s emphasis on reliable delivery over capability claims and materially extends it with concrete procurement tests for measured legal-task errors, recall, reproducibility, security and adversarial robustness. Its vendor responses also illustrate the cluster’s concern that assurances often exceed the supporting evidence.
qs: Hallucinations: measured rates  What is your measured hallucination rate and citation error rate on legal tasks?

Security posture (proof)  Provide current security assurances: independent audit (e.g., SOC 2 Type II or equivalent),  encryption at rest/in transit, SSO/MFA, pen tests, and incident response / breach notification   Everything is encrypted and we are working to SOC 2 Type II certification.

Legal reliability: Mitigation cannot eliminate verification

kp.k: Vendor says customer data never trains models
kp.d: BearisterAI states categorically that user data is not used to train models. The response does not describe fine-tuning, other model-improvement uses, metadata treatment, or any opt-in arrangement.
qs: We do not train any models using user data.

kp.k: Encryption purportedly prevents vendor access to interactions
kp.d: The vendor says user interaction data is protected by end-to-end encryption and is not visible to it. The response does not provide the requested details about role-based access controls, exceptional access, approvals, contractors, or audit logging.
qs: User interaction data is protected under transparent end to end encryption. We cannot see user data.

kp.d: BearisterAI states that it has a zero-retention policy, without specifying separately whether documents, embeddings, prompts, outputs, operational logs, or backups are retained or how hard deletion is implemented.
qs: We have zero data retention policy.

kp.k: Restricted criminal data purportedly remains inaccessible and unstored
kp.d: The vendor says it neither stores, logs, nor accesses CJIS-, CHRI-, or CORI-related data. The response does not describe contractual commitments, subcontractor restrictions, or technical handling controls.
qs: We do not store, log, or access CJIS / CHRI / CORI.

kp.k: Factual outputs purportedly require source citations
kp.d: BearisterAI claims that every factual claim can be traced to an original citation and that the product follows a no-citation, no-claim constraint. No test results or description of citation granularity are supplied.
qs: Yes all the factual claims can be back tracked to an original citation and if no cite no claim.

kp.k: Non-LLM case search is claimed never to hallucinate
kp.d: The vendor says its case-law search feature has no LLM integration and therefore never hallucinates. This claim is limited to that feature; the response provides no measured hallucination rate, citation-error rate, test methodology, or results for other legal tasks.
qs: Our case law search feature does not have any LLM integrations so it never hallucinates

kp.d: BearisterAI says it continues researching recall improvements and claims to be “40% better” than market tools. The response does not identify the comparator products, recall metric, dataset, sample size, evaluation method, or treatment of unprocessed and low-confidence material.
qs: We’re always researching ways of improving our recall; we are 40% better than the market tools

kp.k: Reproducibility claim is conditional and approximate
kp.d: The vendor says later answers will contain generally the same content if the law has not changed. The response does not claim exact reproducibility or describe versioning of models, prompts, or retrieval indexes.
qs: Yes assuming the law has not changed in the interim, the answer will be generally the same content.

kp.k: SOC 2 Type II certification remains in progress
kp.d: BearisterAI states that everything is encrypted and that it is working toward SOC 2 Type II certification. It does not claim current certification or provide the requested details about SSO, MFA, penetration testing, incident response, or breach notification.
qs: Everything is encrypted and we are working to SOC 2 Type II certification.

kp.k: Malformed-PDF effects are claimed to remain user-isolated
kp.d: On adversarial robustness, the vendor says a bad PDF would affect only the uploading user’s output rather than all users. The response does not describe defenses or test results for prompt injection, poisoned documents, or malformed files.
qs: If a bad PDF is uploaded, it will only affect the output of a particular user not all users

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: BearisterAI claims citation-grounded factual outputs, hallucination-free case-law search, improved discovery recall, and broadly repeatable answers.
pts.d: In its vendor responses for BearisterAI 1.0, BearisterAI states that all factual claims can be traced to original citations and that claims without citations are not made. It attributes its claim of no hallucinations specifically to its case-law search feature having no LLM integrations, rather than making that assertion explicitly about every product feature. In response to a discovery-recall question, it claims to be 40% better than market tools, without defining the comparison metric. It also claims that answers will generally retain the same content if the law has not changed. These are product-capability assertions, not predictions about profession-wide employment, pricing, or market restructuring.

pts.k: BearisterAI claims privacy and security controls intended to govern the use of sensitive legal data.
pts.d: The vendor states that it does not train models on user data, cannot see user data because of encryption, maintains zero data retention, and does not store, log, or access CJIS/CHRI/CORI data. It says everything is encrypted and that SOC 2 Type II certification is being pursued, not already held. Its response on adversarial robustness claims that a bad uploaded PDF affects only the particular user's output, rather than all users; it does not claim that the affected user's output remains uncompromised.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The source offers vendor self-reports, architectural explanations, and policy links, but no accompanying empirical results or independent audit findings.
pts.d: BearisterAI offers the absence of LLM integrations as the explanation for its case-law search hallucination claim, but provides no measured hallucination or citation-error rates or testing protocol. The 40% comparative claim is not accompanied by named comparator tools, a dataset, benchmark design, or results. Encryption is offered as the explanation for inability to access user data. The document lists privacy-policy and terms-and-conditions links, whose contents are not reproduced. No independent security audit, reproducibility demonstration, or adversarial test results are supplied in the text. These assertions belong to BearisterAI, not UC Berkeley or the programme, which expressly disclaims endorsement.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: Most assertions describe current BearisterAI 1.0 capabilities in a 2026 pre-demo submission; repeatability is conditional and certification remains prospective.
pts.d: The form identifies BearisterAI 1.0 and a proposed demo date of March 13, 2026, situating the claims without establishing a precise submission date. Citation grounding, data handling, hallucination avoidance, and comparative recall are presented as existing capabilities. Repeatability is qualified by unchanged law and promises only generally similar content, not exact output reproduction. Recall improvement is described as ongoing research. SOC 2 Type II certification is a work in progress with no completion deadline. The bad-PDF containment claim applies when such a file is uploaded.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The claims are directed at public defenders evaluating tools for legal research, discovery review, and handling sensitive client information.
pts.d: Public defender offices and their users are the explicit evaluation audience. The asserted citation traceability, case-law search reliability, discovery recall, and repeatability concern their ability to find and check information used in criminal defense work. Privacy, retention, and criminal-history-data assertions concern sensitive information handled by those offices, with implications for represented clients, although the vendor does not claim measured improvements in client outcomes. The PDF response distinguishes the uploading user's exposure from other users' exposure. The source offers no concrete prediction about staffing changes, cost savings, access-to-justice expansion, or displacement of lawyers.
